Southeast: younger, softer sedimentary rocks (chalk, clay); flatter relief; e.g. London Basin, East Anglia.
Diagonal line dividing UK between upland west/north and lowland south/east; reflects geological boundary.

walkthroughs.body_html:
The Changing Landscapes of the UK — a core area of GCSE Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

The Changing Landscapes of the UK brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with The Changing Landscapes of the UK.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which line divides upland and lowland Britain?
options: Watford Line
Tees-Exe Line
Hadrian's Wall
Severn-Trent Line

mcqs.q: Where are softer sedimentary rocks found in UK?
options: Scottish Highlands
Southeast England
Snowdonia
Lake District

mcqs.q: Why do some rivers form deltas and others form estuaries?
options: Deltas form in cold climates and estuaries in warm climates.
Deltas form where rivers deposit sediment faster than the sea can remove it (calm seas, heavy load); estuaries form where tidal energy removes sediment (strong tides).
Because rainforest soils are made of clay.
Deltas form on big rivers and estuaries on small ones.

mcqs.q: Why are tropical rainforest soils typically infertile?
options: Because so much vegetation grows there, the soil must be fertile.
Because rainforest soils are made of clay.
Urban heat islands only happen in summer.
Heavy rainfall leaches nutrients, and most nutrients are stored in living biomass and rapidly recycled — the soil itself holds very little.

mcqs.q: Why is the urban heat island effect strongest at night?
options: Concrete and brick released their stored daytime heat slowly into the night air, while rural areas cool rapidly through radiative loss — widening the urban-rural temperature gap after sunset.
Because rainforest soils are made of clay.
Urban heat islands only happen in summer.
Urban heat islands are strongest at midday because cities are sunniest then.
